description: Somos el grupo BLACKMOON ENDURENCE del Instituto Tecnológico de Zacatepec
summary:
ENDURENCE is an integrated hardware and software system designed for the continuous health monitoring of astronauts during space missions. It combines a wearable biometric wristband with a web platform that records and displays critical parameters such as cardiovascular rate, oxygen levels, radiation exposure, sleep hours, and physical activity.  
Its importance lies in the fact that long-duration missions expose the crew to severe risks—radiation, microgravity, and isolation—without on-site physicians and with inherent delays in space communications. This constant tracking allows for the early detection of anomalies, the issuance of critical status alerts, and immediate operational recommendations to prevent emergencies and protect crew members' lives.  
To address the challenge of creating space health-monitoring software, a store-and-forward transmission architecture was implemented: the wristband collects the astronaut's biometric data and sends it to the spacecraft, where it is stored for subsequent transmission to Earth. This enables mission control to access and supervise the crew member's health status through a web interface featuring a visual body model.
details:
How does it work?
The ENDURENCE project consists of two main action elements: a wearable biometric wristband and a software platform. The wristband is responsible for monitoring the astronaut and collecting health data to be analyzed both on the spacecraft and on Earth. The wristband first connects to the spacecraft's systems (allowing the crew to view and store the information) and subsequently transmits it to Earth so that the mission control team can also perform a thorough analysis.

What are the benefits?
The main benefit of ENDURENCE is the ability to monitor and analyze astronauts' health in a completely non-invasive way. Additionally, the system allows for the collection of valuable biometric data to drive future medical research on how the human body reacts in space. Most importantly, by detecting anomalies early on, it helps prevent high-risk situations, safeguarding the physical integrity of the astronauts and even preventing fatal consequences.

What is the project's expected impact?
The primary impact of our project centers on providing a technologically innovative solution that makes health monitoring a practical and accessible process. In addition to being efficient and easily portable, the connection between the wearable device and the digital platform allows for operation from anywhere in the world.

Languages

• JavaScript (JSX): The main language. All logic and views are built in .jsx files using React.
• HTML: The page structure, written inside JSX and index.html.
• CSS: Styling, handled with Tailwind CSS v4 and some custom CSS (index.css, App.css).
• SQL (PostgreSQL): Database tables, security policies, and functions, such as astronautas.sql, alarmas.sql, and oficial.sql.
• JSON: Configuration files, such as package.json and vercel.json.

Which tools, programming languages, hardware, or software are used to develop your project?
Libraries and Tools

• React: Used to build component-based views.
• Vite: Development server and bundler.
• React Router: Handles navigation between pages (/, /demo, /monitoreo, etc.).
• Tailwind CSS: Utility-first styling written directly in the code.
• Chart.js: Used for the electrocardiogram chart.
• Lucide: Icons.

Services

• Supabase: PostgreSQL database, authentication, real-time updates, and photo storage.
• Brevo: Handles confirmation emails.
• Vercel: Hosts the live website.
• GitHub: Code repository.

In what sense is our project creative?
The project is creative due to the use of software and hardware for information collection and its subsequent analysis. Furthermore, its synchronization with the spacecraft allows for improved transmission of medical data to Earth, in addition to the fact that the wristband is comfortable and easy to put on and take off.

What factors did the team take into account?
In the project, we took into account the astronaut's comfort, communication with the spacecraft, the dangers of space, and the important data to analyze and collect. We also considered the possibility of use in space and the challenges of this environment, along with its limitations.
